title: Memoization Basics
description: Understand when and how to use React.memo, useMemo, and useCallback to optimize React rendering performance.

data.text: React components re-render whenever their state or props change. While this is the core of React's declarative model, unnecessary re-renders can degrade performance, especially in large applications. Understanding when re-renders happen is the first step toward writing high-performance React code.

data.title: Typical Triggers
items: Parent component re-renders, passing new prop objects or arrays to children
Inline function definitions in JSX, which create new references on every render
Lack of memoization on expensive pure components that receive unchanged props
State updates in components that do not affect the rendered output

data.text: Memoization is a technique to cache the result of expensive computations so they are only recomputed when dependencies change. React provides three primary APIs for memoization: React.memo for components, useMemo for values, and useCallback for functions.

data.caption: How memoization reduces re-renders
data.definition:
graph TB
    A[Parent Re-renders] --> B{Props Changed?}
    B -->|Yes| C[Re-render Child]
    B -->|No| D[Skip Render]
    C --> E[Expensive Work]
    D --> F[Reuse Cached Output]

data.text: React.memo is a higher-order component that wraps a functional component and prevents it from re-rendering if its props have not changed. It performs a shallow comparison of props by default.

data.title: Wrapping a Component with React.memo
data.content: Use React.memo when a component renders often with the same props.

data.title: Shallow Comparison Limit
data.text: React.memo only shallow-compares props. If you pass objects, arrays, or functions, it will still re-render when the reference changes, even if the internal data is identical. Use useMemo or useCallback to stabilize those references.

useMemo caches the result of a calculation between renders. It only recomputes the cached value when one of its dependencies changes. This is useful for expensive calculations like filtering large arrays, sorting data, or parsing JSON.

data.title: Memoizing an Expensive Calculation
data.content: Suppose we filter a large list of products on every render.

data.title: When to Use useMemo
data.text: Only use useMemo for expensive computations. For simple values, the overhead of memoization can outweigh the benefit. Profile first, optimize second.

useCallback returns a memoized callback function. Like useMemo, it only changes the function reference when its dependencies change. This is essential when passing callbacks to optimized child components wrapped in React.memo.

data.title: Stabilizing Event Handlers
data.content: Without useCallback, the handleRemove reference changes on every render and breaks React.memo optimization.

cards.title: React.memo
cards.description: Wraps a component to skip re-renders when props are shallowly equal.
cons: Does not help local state updates

cards.title: useMemo
cards.description: Caches the result of an expensive calculation between renders.

cards.title: useCallback
cards.description: Returns a memoized callback that only changes when dependencies change.

data.text: Not every component needs memoization. Overusing these hooks adds mental overhead and can sometimes hurt performance due to the cost of comparison and cache management. Always measure with React DevTools Profiler before and after applying memoization.

data.title: Practice: Profile and Memoize
data.description: Open a React app in DevTools Profiler. Find a component that re-renders frequently with the same props. Apply React.memo, useMemo, or useCallback and measure the improvement.
steps: Open React DevTools and switch to the Profiler tab
Click Record and interact with your app for a few seconds
Identify a component with high render count but unchanged props
Wrap it in React.memo and record again
If props include objects or callbacks, stabilize them with useMemo and useCallback
Compare render counts before and after
data.expectedOutcome: You should see fewer renders for the memoized component while the app still functions correctly.

items.question: Does React.memo guarantee a component will never re-render?
items.answer: No. React.memo only skips re-renders when props are shallowly equal. It does not prevent re-renders caused by local state changes, context changes, or parent re-renders with new prop references.

items.question: Should I wrap every component in React.memo?
items.answer: No. Apply it selectively to components that are expensive to render and receive stable props. Simple presentational components usually do not benefit.

items.question: Can useMemo and useCallback slow down my app?
items.answer: Yes, if overused. They add overhead for storing values in memory and comparing dependencies. Use them for expensive work or when passing callbacks to memoized children.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: React.memo skips re-renders when props are shallowly equal
useMemo caches computed values for expensive operations
useCallback stabilizes function references for memoized children
Measure with React DevTools before applying optimizations
Avoid premature optimization on simple, low-frequency components
